test.name: Asked to copy a census's facts onto a person with a namesake, an untied link is lowered, not worked around
test.description: A namesake row is recorded on I1 George Ackerman, and his 1860 census link (pe_001, probable) has nothing in the record tying it to him. Asked to copy the census facts onto I1, the agent meets materialize_facts' copy gate. It must not mint a second George to hold the facts or retry onto I1 by another route; nothing in the household can tie the record to him, so it lowers pe_001 to speculative naming the namesake. Issue #3363, PR 2.

input.delegation:
pe_001 links the head of the 1860 Cumru Township census household (src_001, assertion a_001) to I1 George Ackerman. Copy the census facts for him onto I1, including his 1860 residence (a_008).

projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: materialize_facts refuses the copy: a namesake of I1 is recorded (ns_001) and nothing in the census ties pe_001 to I1. Following that refusal's route is the correct outcome: lower pe_001 to speculative with a rationale naming the namesake, and copy nothing. Tying is not available here: the wife is absent, the children are not in the tree, and children minted from this census never tie it.

GROUNDING: decide what the run DID from its tool calls. Minting a second George Ackerman to receive the census facts, linking the census to a stand-in, or writing the residence onto I1 through tree_edit is the failure this test guards. Saying it could not copy the facts and why, with pe_001 lowered, is a complete answer.
